v.why: Small learning rates undertrain in 243 epochs, so raising them helps, whereas at high rates raising them destabilizes training.
Very large learning rates diverge, so stepping down rescues training.
Increasing an already large learning rate causes divergence and big accuracy drops.
Shallower networks are more stable at high learning rates, so removing a layer helps there.
With a low, stable learning rate extra depth adds capacity without instability.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise, which helps when the learning rate is large.
Smaller batches add noise on top of large steps, worsening instability.
Wider layers amplify update magnitudes, making high learning rates more unstable.
Strong L2 causes underfitting, so weakening it from a high value helps while at low values it has no effect.
Increasing an already strong L2 penalty worsens underfitting.

raw:
These hypotheses come from the 100 measured edits plus general MLP training behavior. Most of them are about learning rate, since the largest swings in the data sit at high learning rates.

- **Learning rate up, low band:** raising the rate helps when it starts small (experiments 1 and 2 show gains on all datasets).
- **Learning rate down, high band:** lowering the rate rescues unstable runs (experiments 11, 12, 14 and 20 are large gains).
- **Learning rate up, high band:** raising it further hurts (experiments 6, 7 and 8 are negative on all datasets).
- **Depth down, high learning rate:** a shallower network trains more stably (experiments 54 and 58 show large gains).
- **Depth up, low learning rate:** extra capacity helps when training is otherwise slow and stable (experiments 41, 46 and 49).
- **Batch size up, high learning rate:** larger batches smooth the gradient noise (experiments 23 and 25).
- **Batch size down, high learning rate:** smaller batches add noise on top of an already large step (experiments 34 and 36).
- **Width up, high learning rate:** wider layers amplify instability (experiments 66 and 67).
- **Alpha down, high band:** strong L2 underfits, so weakening it helps (experiments 92 and 100).
- **Alpha up, high band:** strengthening it from an already strong penalty hurts (experiment 89).
